headline: Aroldis Chapman makes history as the Red Sox find their rhythm
morning_brew: It was a night to remember at the yard as the Red Sox took down the Angels in a win that we really needed to stop the bleeding. Aroldis Chapman was the story of the night, passing Hoyt Wilhelm to become the all-time leader in strikeouts by a reliever. That is the kind of milestone you stop and appreciate, even when the season hasn't exactly gone the way we all hoped back in April. It took some serious work from the bullpen to nail down the final few frames, but seeing a guy like that etch his name into the record books is something special.

Jake Bennett was absolutely dealing on the mound, keeping the Angels hitters guessing for nearly eight full innings. When you get that kind of performance from your starter, it makes the whole job easier for everyone else in the dugout. Romy Gonzalez and Ceddanne Rafaela were swinging the bats well, putting together solid at-bats that helped us pull ahead and stay there. It felt like the team finally played a complete game where the pitching and the hitting were actually in sync for once.

While we are focused on the diamond, the rest of the Hub is in full offseason mode. The Celtics are busy shuffling the roster and the Bruins are navigating the trade market, but for us, the road trip to Anaheim continues tonight. We have to keep this momentum moving forward because we have a lot of ground to make up in the standings before the summer heat really kicks in. Let's hope the bats stay loud and we can string a few more wins together.

news_digest.headline: Boston's Chapman sets all-time record for strikeouts by reliever
news_digest.dans_take: An incredible feat for a guy who has been mowing hitters down for years.
